Audit Survey Identities and Paired Distance-Removal Counts

Source: R/validate_unmarked_data.R
validate_unmarked_data.Rd

Check an unmarkedFrameGDR against a table of original survey identifiers before you fit a model. The audit looks for split or duplicated surveys, covariates out of line with the surveys, distance and removal counts that disagree, and counts that conflict with survey effort. It only reports. It does not combine surveys, reorder rows, remove records or repair counts.

Usage

validate_unmarked_data(
  object,
  event_keys,
  event_id,
  site_id = NULL,
  interval_units,
  effort = NULL,
  expected_event_keys = NULL
)

# S3 method for class 'msr_unmarked_audit'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

object

An unmarkedFrameGDR holding paired distance and removal counts for point surveys. Other frame classes are not supported.

event_keys

A data frame with one row per survey event, in the frame's order. An event is one primary period at one frame row, so with one visit per point there is one row per frame row. With several primary periods, list all periods of the first frame row, then all periods of the second, and so on. Use the original survey identifiers, such as a point name and date, rather than a row number.

event_id

Character vector naming the columns of event_keys that together identify one survey event. Their combinations should be unique; repeated combinations are reported.

site_id

Optional character vector naming the columns of event_keys that identify the physical site. A site may appear in several events (repeat visits). The default NULL skips the site checks.

interval_units

Character string naming the time unit of object@period.lengths, for example "minutes". Removal probabilities are per unit of this time. The label is recorded, not converted.

effort

Optional numeric vector with one value per event, in event order, such as minutes surveyed. A positive value marks a completed survey, zero marks an event that was not surveyed (its counts must be NA), and NA marks unknown effort. With the default NULL, the audit adds a warning, because counts alone cannot separate a completed survey with no detections from one that never happened.

expected_event_keys

Optional data frame, built independently of event_keys (for example from the field schedule), with the event_id columns in the order the frame should have. Rows whose keys differ are reported. A key table cannot show by itself that it is in the right order.

x

An object returned by validate_unmarked_data().

...

Further arguments passed to the data-frame print method.

Value

A list of class msr_unmarked_audit:

  • valid: TRUE when no errors were found. Warnings can remain, so read them too.

  • findings: a data frame with one row per finding. Columns are severity ("error" or "warning"), code (see "Finding codes"), message, the event's position in frame order (.event), its frame row (.site_row) and primary period (.primary), followed by the event_keys columns for that event. Findings about the whole frame have missing positions.

  • events: event_keys as supplied.

  • summary: the number of frame rows (sites), primary_periods, events, errors and warnings, and missing_histories, the number of events with both count tables fully missing.

  • protocol: distance_units, interval_units, distance_breaks and interval_lengths from the frame.

  • effort: the supplied effort vector.

Printing shows the error and warning counts and at most ten findings, and returns the object invisibly. The full table stays in $findings.

Identify survey events and physical sites

A physical site can be visited more than once. Give each visit its own event identifier, and keep the site in a separate column named by site_id. A row number from a spreadsheet cannot show that a detection record and a zero-detection record belong to the same survey, so resolve survey identities when you build the frame from the original records, for example with prepare_gdr_histories().

The distance and removal tables count the same birds, so their totals must match for each event. Matching totals are necessary but cannot reveal a survey split across two frame rows. Supplying the original event keys lets the audit report such a split as duplicate_event. Key names that look like row indices (such as index, row_id or X) give a warning. When an event_id or site_id column also appears in the site, yearly or observation covariates, its values are compared with event_keys row by row. Without expected_event_keys or such shared columns, unique keys alone cannot prove that the rows are aligned.

Record survey effort

A survey that took place and detected nothing is an observed zero. A survey that never took place should have fully missing counts in both tables. Supply effort so the audit can tell these apart. Counts that are missing in only one table, or in only some columns, are reported because their totals cannot be compared. Character and factor values, including the literal string "None", are kept as values and not treated as missing.

Finding codes

CodeSeverityMeaning
frame_layouterrorThe count tables do not have matching rows and complete primary-period blocks. Other checks are skipped
survey_typeerrorThe frame is not a point survey
event_layouterrorevent_keys does not have one row per event. Other checks are skipped
missing_event_keyerrorAn event identifier is missing or blank
duplicate_eventerrorOne event key appears in more than one event, as when a survey is split
index_like_event_keywarningAn event_id column name looks like a row index
missing_site_keyerrorA site identifier is missing or blank
physical_site_alignmenterrorPrimary periods in one frame row have different site keys
event_alignmenterrorThe key differs from expected_event_keys in that row
duplicate_reference_eventerrorexpected_event_keys repeats an event
covariate_layouterrorA covariate table has the wrong number of rows or repeated names
covariate_key_alignmenterrorA key column in a covariate table differs from event_keys
response_slot_alignmenterrorThe frame's response and removal tables disagree
distance_breakserrorDistance breaks do not start at zero, increase, and match the distance columns
distance_unitserrorDistance units are not "m" or "km"
interval_lengthserrorInterval lengths are not positive whole numbers, one per removal column
invalid_countserrorA count is negative, fractional, infinite or NaN
partial_historyerrorAn event's counts are only partly missing
unequal_totalserrorDistance and removal totals differ for the event
effort_unspecifiedwarningNo effort was supplied
invalid_efforterrorEffort is negative or infinite
unsurveyed_countserrorAn event with zero effort has counts, including zeros
surveyed_missingerrorAn event with positive effort has fully missing counts
unknown_effortwarningEffort is NA for the event

The audit does not decide how to treat a bird first detected beyond the survey radius and later inside it, or how to turn raw bird records into counts. prepare_gdr_histories() handles that step. See the "Check that the records line up with the surveys" section of vignette("v12-distance-removal", package = "multiScaleR") for the audit in a full workflow.

See also

prepare_gdr_histories(), prepare_gdr_intervals(), expand_gdr_intervals(), sim_dat_gdr()

Examples

# Two visits to site A, one frame row each, with matching totals
frame <- unmarked::unmarkedFrameGDR(
  yDistance = matrix(c(1, 0, 0, 0), 2, byrow = TRUE),
  yRemoval = matrix(c(0, 1, 0, 0), 2, byrow = TRUE),
  dist.breaks = c(0, 25, 75), unitsIn = "m",
  period.lengths = c(1, 2))
keys <- data.frame(site = c("A", "A"), visit = c("spring", "summer"))
audit <- validate_unmarked_data(frame, keys, c("site", "visit"),
  site_id = "site", interval_units = "minutes", effort = c(3, 3))
audit$valid      # TRUE: no errors and, with effort supplied, no warnings
#> [1] TRUE
audit
#> GDR survey audit: 2 events; 0 errors; 0 warnings

# Give both rows the same key, as if one survey had been split in two.
# Their totals still match, but the event mapping is now invalid.
split_keys <- keys
split_keys$visit[2] <- "spring"
split_audit <- validate_unmarked_data(frame, split_keys, c("site", "visit"),
  site_id = "site", interval_units = "minutes", effort = c(3, 3))
split_audit$valid
#> [1] FALSE
split_audit$findings[, c("severity", "code", ".event", "visit")]
#>   severity            code .event  visit
#> 1    error duplicate_event      1 spring
#> 2    error duplicate_event      2 spring
